source.title: The Unlearning Mirage: A Dynamic Framework for Evaluating LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Raj Sanjay Shah; Jing Huang; K. Murugesan; Nathalie Baracaldo; Diyi Yang

record.file_problem: No major file problem; the full paper and appendices are present. Some table formatting is flattened, but the main results can be assigned.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether unlearning leaves knowledge accessible using a dynamic, model-informed evaluation and activation-pathway analysis, rather than the original studies’ evaluation methods.
record.gate_note: The paper’s own unlearning results and query-variation tests are included. Comparisons and results cited from other work are not rows. Knowledge-graph sizes, benchmark coverage, and correlation with prior rankings do not directly measure the claim. The PatchScopes layer-resolution observations are included because they bear on whether unlearning disrupts access pathways.
record.test_reason: The study applies 12 unlearning methods to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, with Phi-4-mini and Granite-3.2-8B in the appendix, on RWKU and TOFU entities. It measures residual accuracy on direct, multi-hop, aliased and decomposed queries built from the model's own pre-unlearning knowledge. These results bear on A (how much knowledge remains after unlearning) and E (recovery by rephrasing). A qualitative PatchScopes look also bears on C. This is a different method aimed at the same question. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is right but incomplete. The authors conclude that existing unlearning methods are brittle: multi-hop and aliased queries recover supposedly forgotten facts that static single-hop benchmarks miss. Their dynamic knowledge-graph framework matches prior benchmarks' coverage (about 78% of RWKU, 66% of TOFU) and their method rankings (Spearman 0.87 removal on RWKU). Step-by-step decomposition makes negligible difference. On MUSE-Books, GA and NPO score 0 on prior verbatim and knowledge metrics yet keep multi-hop accuracy. The authors offer the PatchScopes finding only as a qualitative candidate explanation: single-hop answers resolve in middle layers that unlearning disrupts, while multi-hop targets resolve later through intact paths.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a dynamic knowledge-graph evaluation and PatchScopes analysis; evaluates several unlearning methods but does not reproduce the original studies’ attack recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Query complexity changes residual retrieval: multi-hop accuracy rises from 1-hop to 2-hop to 3-hop on average. Aliasing intermediate entities raises average 2-hop accuracy by 2.4%; step-by-step decomposition has negligible effect, as described by the authors.

fits_no_version.finding: Unintended forgetting grows with knowledge-graph proximity to the target. Related-fact retention averages 61.7 one fact away vs 67.7 two facts away on RWKU (target 98.9/98.1). TOFU shows the same, at 60.4 vs 66.9 in Table 7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning's collateral damage concentrates on facts adjacent to the target in the knowledge graph.

record.problems: No never-trained or never-saw-knowledge comparison and no stated chance level. Generic capability retention is not directly evaluated in the main results; retention tests are related facts and relations. PatchScopes analysis is qualitative, limited to an example, and the method used for that activation analysis is not stated. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated accuracies.
record.rows_left_out: The 1-hop post-unlearning values for each method in Table 2, the per-method 1-hop results and related-fact retention columns in Tables 2, 4, 5, and 7, and the per-method results in the MUSE-Books table were left out to stay within the 60-row cap. They are not needed to represent the multi-hop and prompt-variation results retained here.

untested.parts: No chance level and no never-trained comparison. General ability is measured only through KG-based related-fact and relation retention (plus MUSE utility in the appendix), not generic benchmarks such as MMLU. RMU and WMDP-style hazardous knowledge are not tested; the authors say elicitation struggles there.
No relearning fine-tuning of any kind.
No activation-direction ablation or other causal test. The PatchScopes evidence is one qualitative, selected example.
No jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context provision of facts. Only multi-hop composition, entity aliasing and step-by-step decomposition are tested.

missing.what: Per-method 2-hop and 3-hop residual accuracy for Phi-4-mini-instruct (3.8B) and Granite-3.2-8B-Instruct on RWKU (2-hop 22.2-47.8 and 17.6-45.9; 3-hop 31.5-57.4 and 26.9-52.6). These repeat the residual-knowledge pattern on two more models.
The same Phi-4-mini and Granite multi-hop columns, with their per-method 1-hop values (avg 23.1 and 19.8) as baselines. Multi-hop exceeds 1-hop on both models (avg 30.3/37.3 and 27.2/32.7).
Per-method 2-hop and 3-hop residual accuracy on TOFU for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (2-hop 20.1-41.1, 3-hop 28.9-51.1; target 86.3/78.6)
TOFU per-method multi-hop vs 1-hop accuracy for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (avg 1-hop 20.6, 2-hop 26.8, 3-hop 33.7)

Per-method post-unlearning 1-hop (direct query) accuracy on RWKU: 11.2-28.3, avg 20.1, vs 98.6 before. This is the most direct test of A's near-chance claim. rows_left_out declares it, but no row records it.
The same per-method 1-hop values, needed as each multi-hop row's baseline for E. The rows use the target model as baseline instead.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) The merge refused the earlier verdict because of the record's undeclared V1-V6 codes, and its row_fixes also grouped several rows per item. Each group is now split into one item per row, r1-r52. Codes were remapped by what each row measures: V1 to A, V3 to C, V5 to E; r1-r2 to none. Each 2-hop and 3-hop row now names its own method's 1-hop baseline from Table 2.
(2) The aliasing gain range is corrected from +0.2..+5.2 to +1.2..+5.2.
(3) The E label on r3-r26 is changed from supports to limits_scope. Those rows are partial: multi-hop beats direct queries for every method, but only reaches about 28-40% of pre-unlearning accuracy, so "restores it" is overstated.
(4) The single surface-variant E label is split into two condition groups, aliasing (partial) and decomposition (absent).
(5) The missing entries are split so each carries a single declared version identifier.
(6) Added to A's untested parts: RMU and WMDP are not tested.
(7) The C reason now notes that the PatchScopes example was selected for multi-hop failure.
(8) The MUSE-Books range is corrected: GA and NPO multi-hop accuracy is 7.0-26.4, not 7-36.
Other notes: Probes are scored only if the pre-unlearning model answered them, yet target-model accuracies are below 100 (98.6/97.2/84.1); the paper does not explain this. The 1-hop, 2-hop and 3-hop sets are different questions, so multi-hop vs 1-hop comparisons cross question sets. Answers are open-ended, so chance is near 0; this is our inference, as the paper states no chance level. No uncertainty is reported (means of 3 runs). MUSE-Books (Table 11) is declared left out but is strong for A and E: GA and NPO show 0 verbatim and knowledge scores but 9.2-26.4 and 7.0-24.1 multi-hop accuracy. Their MUSE utility is also 0, a cost against A's 'keeping general ability'. The text's 'minimum multi-hop accuracy of 9.6%' for GA does not match Table 11: 9.6 is ICL's average removal score, and GA's is 19.2. The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare with a model that never learned the knowledge, state a chance level, or evaluate generic capabilities directly; retention tests are related facts and relations.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or causal intervention; pathway analysis is qualitative and does not establish deletion versus blocked access conclusively.
Tests aliasing of intermediate entities and step-by-step decomposition on two-hop queries; no jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context knowledge provided to restore facts.
No newer counter-method claimed to resist these attacks.
